water.name: Land
water.rule: Most of the hex's 7 sample points (centre + 6) are outside the BFS G1 lakes.

water.name: Ocean
water.rule: Not used: Switzerland has no sea.

water.name: Lake
water.rule: At least 4 of the hex's 7 sample points fall in a BFS G1 lake (lakes over about 5 km², border lakes in full), unless the hex holds 500+ residents and at least 2 land samples (a lakeside village or city).

relief.name: Flat
relief.rule: Height spread (standard deviation) inside the hex under 30 m.

relief.name: Mountains
relief.rule: Height spread ≥ 110 m, or mean height ≥ 1,400 m.

relief.name: Peaks
relief.rule: Mean height ≥ 2,200 m, or highest point ≥ 3,000 m with a spread ≥ 200 m (high Alps).

cover.name: None
cover.rule: Water, foreign land, or no land-cover points.

cover.name: Deciduous forest
cover.rule: Forest is the largest group and the hex's mean height is under 700 m.

cover.name: Conifer forest
cover.rule: Forest is the largest group and the hex's mean height is 1,100 m or more.

cover.name: Mixed forest
cover.rule: Forest is the largest group, mean height 700 to 1,100 m.

cover.name: Brush forest
cover.rule: Brush forest (Gebüschwald) is the largest group.

cover.name: Alpine pasture & meadow
cover.rule: Alpine farmland, unproductive vegetation and parks are the largest group.

cover.name: Meadows & pasture
cover.rule: Meadows and farm pastures are the largest group.

cover.name: Arable land & vineyards
cover.rule: Arable land, orchards, vineyards and horticulture are the largest group.

cover.name: Settlement
cover.rule: Settlement and transport areas are ≥ 30% of the hex's land, whatever else is there.

cover.name: Rock & scree
cover.rule: Bare land (rock, scree, sand) is the largest group.

cover.name: Glacier & firn
cover.rule: Glaciers and perpetual snow are the largest group.

notes.water: Lakes are the BFS generalised (G1) lake outlines; smaller lakes and rivers are narrower than a hex and are land. A mostly-lake hex with residents on its shore stays land, so lakeside villages show on the map.
notes.relief: From swisstopo DHM25/200 heights read every 400 m (about 70 samples per hex).
notes.cover: From the BFS land use statistics (Arealstatistik, newest survey per hectare point), read on a 400 m lattice. Lakes and rivers are ignored; shares are of the remaining land points. Foreign hexes have no land cover.
